source: Nair, Gizzi, Sinapov (2024) Creative Problem Solving in Large Language and Vision Models - What Would it Take?
finding: Position paper that ties Boden's exploratory creativity to search over LLM outputs. It names tree-of-thought, MCTS and beam search as existing exploratory methods but says none were built to cover a conceptual space or applied to embedding spaces.
numbers: No headline numbers for the argument. It cites a podcast remark that real creative problem solving needs search.
limits: Argument, not an experiment. The authors call their own tests preliminary. Conceptual space is mapped to embedding space with no validation.
agent_relevance: Backs the S3 idea that search over candidates is the exploratory operator. Says nothing about how much it helps.

source: Nair, Gizzi, Sinapov (2024) Creative Problem Solving in Large Language and Vision Models - What Would it Take?
finding: Only experiment: object replacement with vision-language models (CLIP variants, ViLT, LLaVA). Pick the object that can stand in for a missing tool (bowl for scoop, saucepan for hammer, knife for spatula, safety pin for toothpick, scissors for pliers).
numbers: 4 candidate images per test, 10 test sets per core object, 50 samples per model. Random pick about 30% (author figure). Nominal case (tool present): CLIP-B-32 100%, B-16 92%, L-14 98%, H-14-laion 98%, ViLT 68%, LLaVA 98%. Replacement case with plain prompt: reported as poor in a figure.
limits: Replacement targets were chosen by the authors themselves. Tiny sample, no stats tests. Exact replacement-case values are only in a figure that was not read as numbers.
agent_relevance: Models that know the normal use of a thing fail when the use must be re-framed. Matches fixation findings.

source: Nair, Gizzi, Sinapov (2024) Creative Problem Solving in Large Language and Vision Models - What Would it Take?
finding: Adding object-affordance text (shape features) to the prompt, a stand-in for task re-representation from the creativity literature, gave a general improvement over the plain prompt. Task-only and task-plus-affordance prompts were also tried.
numbers: Four prompt types tested on each model. Improvement is described as general; per-model values are in Figure 2 only.
limits: Preliminary, small, scoring models (CLIP) not chat models. No replication found.
agent_relevance: Supports an S3 step that re-describes the problem in terms of needed functions before searching for candidates.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
finding: Search over a tree of partial thoughts (generate, vote or score, keep the best b) beat plain and chain-of-thought prompts on Game of 24 with GPT-4.
numbers: Game of 24: IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, ToT b=1 45%, ToT b=5 74%. Best of 100 CoT samples: 49%. ToT uses about 5.5k completion tokens per case, close to 100 CoT trials (6.7k), at lower cost than best-of-100 CoT per the paper's cost table.
limits: Game of 24 is a checkable puzzle, not open-ended creativity. Costs several times a single prompt.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that deliberate search beats equal-budget sampling when an evaluator is reliable. Core S3 argument.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: Creative writing task (four random sentences must end four paragraphs): plan-then-write search with 5 plans voted on, then 5 passages voted on.
numbers: GPT-4 coherence score (1-10, 100 tasks): IO 6.19, CoT 6.93, ToT 7.56. Humans preferred ToT over CoT in 41 of 100 pairs, CoT over ToT in 21, 38 similar. Iterative refine lifted IO 6.19 to 7.67 and ToT 7.56 to 7.91.
limits: Metric is coherence from an LLM judge, not novelty or value. Refinement alone gave a bigger gain for IO than tree search did.
agent_relevance: Search helps coherence of open text, but a plain refine loop is cheaper and nearly as good. Do not oversell search for creative text.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts (appendix B.2)
finding: Which half of search matters: generating candidates or judging them. Mixing GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 in Game of 24 showed the bottleneck was generation.
numbers: GPT-3.5 ToT 19% vs GPT-4 ToT 74%. GPT-4 generate + GPT-3.5 evaluate 64%. GPT-3.5 generate + GPT-4 evaluate 31%.
limits: One task, two models.
agent_relevance: A cheap judge can be enough if the generator is strong. Spend the strong model on proposals.

source: Hao et al. (2023) Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP)
finding: MCTS where the LLM is both proposer and world model beat chain-of-thought and self-consistency on planning and math.
numbers: Blocksworld: CoT 29.4, CoT+SC(10) 46.8, RAP(1) 48.6, RAP(10) 51.6 (success %). Abstract: LLaMA-33B with RAP beats GPT-4 with CoT, a 33% relative gain. GSM8K: RAP 48.8%. ProntoQA: pred acc CoT 87.8 vs RAP 94.2; proof acc 64.8 vs 78.8.
limits: Planning and logic with checkable goals. Not a creativity test.
agent_relevance: Shows search with state tracking prevents illegal moves. Relevant when the open task has hard constraints.

source: Lehman et al. (2022/2023) Evolution through Large Models
finding: An LLM trained on code acts as the mutation operator inside MAP-Elites (a quality-diversity archive) to invent walking robots (Sodaracers) in a domain the model never saw.
numbers: Stage-1 data: 50%-cutoff set about 280K examples, 80%-cutoff set about 95K. Fine-tuning the diff model on accepted diffs raised the share of valid, runnable diffs and the QD score (Figure 11). A randomly initialised 300M model produced no valid programs.
limits: Sodarace is a toy simulator with a clear fitness. Radial seed gave high QD scores but exploited chaotic physics that overfit flat ground, so QD score alone missed a quality problem.
agent_relevance: Template for generate-and-test creativity: LLM varies, a programmatic evaluator selects, an archive keeps diversity. Needs an automatic check.

source: Lehman et al. (2022/2023) Evolution through Large Models
finding: Seed choice shaped what search found: CPPN seed uncovered diversity fastest, Radial seed gave better average quality, Square and CPPN gave more predictable designs.
numbers: Per-seed QD and max-fitness curves (Figures 9-10). Diminishing returns on a second round of diff-model fine-tuning (preliminary).
limits: Few seeds, no confidence bounds in text.
agent_relevance: Starting points constrain the space searched. An S3 open mode should vary the seed, not just resample.

source: Meyerson et al. (2023) Language Model Crossover
finding: Using an LLM as a crossover operator by prompting with several parent texts produced mostly valid, varied offspring across binary strings, sentences, code and image prompts.
numbers: Percent valid offspring approaches 100% as the number of parents in the prompt grows (text). With Sodaracers, about 30% of offspring valid with the 6B model; larger models gave more niches filled and higher QD score. LMX and LMX-Near gave higher QD than baselines (Mann-Whitney p<0.05).
limits: Small domains. Authors admit LMX does not solve premature convergence or exploration-exploitation trade-offs.
agent_relevance: Cheap way to get variation in an agent loop: show 2-4 candidate ideas and ask for a new one.

source: Bradley et al. (2024) Quality-Diversity through AI Feedback (QDAIF)
finding: An LLM generates and also rates quality and diversity traits (e.g. sentiment of an opinion, genre of a story) inside MAP-Elites, so no hand-made metric is needed.
numbers: Human study, averages over opinions, story genre, story ending (small n). Human QD score: QDAIF 0.772, Fixed-Few-Shot 0.767, Shuffling-Few-Shot 0.696, LMX quality-only 0.650, Random-Search 0.606. Human quality rating 3.9 (QDAIF) vs 4.133 (Fixed-Few-Shot). Computed QD score: QDAIF beat all baselines in the paper's plots.
limits: On human evaluation QDAIF is only about equal to the fixed few-shot baseline and had lower mean quality rating. The win is in computed QD score, which uses the same AI feedback that guides the search.
agent_relevance: Judge-guided archives widen coverage but a human check shows little gain over a good fixed prompt. Treat self-judged gains with caution.

source: Franceschelli and Musolesi (2024) Creative Beam Search: LLM-as-a-Judge for Improving Response Generation
finding: Generate with Diverse Beam Search then have the same LLM pick the most creative of 4 candidates, a simulation of production then response phases.
numbers: Llama 2 7B chat, beam budget 8, 8 groups, top K=4. 31 graduate students, 217 answers: CBS preferred 45%, standard sampling 29%, too similar to tell 26%. Output equalled plain DBS output in 29% of cases.
limits: Qualitative, no creativity test, small model, one-quarter of pairs indistinguishable. Authors name the need for a broader evaluation.
agent_relevance: Generate-diverse-then-self-judge is cheap but gives a modest user preference. Fits S3 but not a big lever.

source: Lu et al. (2024) The AI Scientist
finding: An LLM agent loop of idea generation, a novelty check against the literature, coding, experiments, and automated review, run on templates from three ML subfields.
numbers: Cost under $15 per paper. Automated reviewer scored some papers above a weak-accept threshold. Reviews cost $0.25 to $0.50 each. Smaller models gave far worse review performance.
limits: Novelty check is self-assessed by the model. Failure modes listed include hallucinated experimental details (for example claiming V100 GPUs) and overrating of an idea's interestingness and novelty.
agent_relevance: Full agent loop with a novelty filter and a reviewer. Shows the failure of unverified self-judged novelty.

source: Romera-Paredes et al. (2024) Mathematical discoveries from program search with LLMs (FunSearch)
finding: Pair a pretrained LLM with a systematic evaluator in an evolutionary loop that searches for programs, not answers. Found larger cap sets than the best known.
numbers: Found a set of 512 eight-dimensional cap set vectors, a new best in dimension 8 (page text), plus new online bin packing heuristics that beat standard baselines.
limits: Only works when a fast automatic scorer exists. Abstract and part of the page text read; supplementary data not read.
agent_relevance: Strongest proof that LLM plus verifier search can produce new things. The verifier is what makes it work.

source: Novikov et al. / Google DeepMind (2025) AlphaEvolve
finding: FunSearch successor: an LLM ensemble edits whole code files in an evolutionary loop with automatic evaluators.
numbers: 48 scalar multiplications for 4x4 complex matrices, the first improvement over Strassen in 56 years in that setting. Over 50 open math problems: matched best known on 75%, beat state of the art on 20%. Kissing number in 11 dimensions raised from 592 to 593. Production use: heuristic recovers 0.7% of fleet compute; 23% kernel speedup and 1% cut in Gemini training time.
limits: Company report, mostly not independently reproduced. Problems are all machine-checkable.
agent_relevance: Same lesson as FunSearch at larger scale: exploratory search works when there is an oracle.

source: Liu et al. (2024) Evolution of Heuristics (EoH)
finding: Evolve both natural-language 'thoughts' and code. Beat FunSearch on online bin packing with far fewer LLM queries.
numbers: Online bin packing excess-bin gap to lower bound on one test set: First Fit 5.32%, Best Fit 4.87%, FunSearch 3.78%, EoH 2.24%; on another set 6.75% vs 2.13%. EoH uses a few thousand queries; FunSearch reported about 1 million.
limits: Gap values are mixed: on some sets FunSearch ties or wins (0.33% vs 0.61%). Ablation: using only one exploration strategy (EoH-e1) raised gap to 55% on some sets.
agent_relevance: A text-level idea layer makes search far cheaper. Matches a schema step that writes the idea before the answer.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) OMNI-EPIC
finding: Foundation models propose the next task, check it against an archive with a model of interestingness, code the environment, and train an agent.
numbers: Ablations on short runs with learning (uniform in-context sampling, no failed examples, no learning-progress notion) are in Figures 33-35; read as captions only, no numbers taken.
limits: Interestingness is whatever the model thinks is interesting. No human agreement numbers read.
agent_relevance: Archive plus novelty-compared-to-neighbours filter is a reusable loop piece for generating non-duplicate candidates.

source: Tian et al. (2024) MacGyver: Are Large Language Models Creative Problem Solvers?
finding: 1,600+ problems that need unusual object use. Humans and LLMs fail in different ways. Humans fail when the item is outside their experience; LLMs propose physically infeasible steps.
numbers: GPT-4 baseline: 18.9% efficient solution, 37.5% infeasible. Majority-vote human 79.3% correct vs GPT-4 73.3% on solvable problems. Error types: wrong tool use 42.4%, goal not reached 17.7%, unneeded steps 16.9%, unfaithful to constraints 9.5%.
limits: Dataset made by LLM then cleaned. Judging used humans and LLMs; self-reflection did not help Claude 2 or Llama 2.
agent_relevance: Dominant failure is infeasible steps, which a feasibility check in the loop can catch.

source: Tian et al. (2024) MacGyver
finding: Two scaffolds on GPT-4: Self-Reflect (verify feasibility of steps) and Divergent-Convergent Thinking (list possible uses first, then choose).
numbers: Self-Reflect cut infeasible solutions by 9.7 points; Div-Conv by 4.3. Div-Conv raised efficient solutions by 6.5 points; Self-Reflect by 2.2. Div-Conv helped all three models; Self-Reflect did not help Claude 2 or Llama 2.
limits: Single paper, three models, effects of a few points.
agent_relevance: Explore-then-filter scaffold is a small but model-general gain. Self-check depends on model strength.

source: Lu et al. (2024) Benchmarking Language Model Creativity: A Case Study on Code Generation (Denial Prompting)
finding: Repeatedly forbid the technique used in the last solution to force a new region of the solution space. Already summarised in the Boden subfield document (C04.01); recorded here only as the drop-a-rule search move.
numbers: See C04.01 DEEP.md: pass@1 16.1% falling to 2.1% over 0-5 forbidden techniques; MCTS the only reasoning strategy to raise divergent creativity.
limits: Overlap with C04.01 by design. Not independent evidence.
agent_relevance: Constraint-adding as a way to push search elsewhere.

source: Cross-paper reading of c04, c05, c13, c14, c16
finding: Pattern across the machine studies: search wins by large margins when an oracle exists (Game of 24, cap sets, bin packing, matrix multiplication) and by small or mixed margins when only an LLM judge exists.
numbers: ToT Game of 24 +66 points over IO; creative writing coherence 6.19 to 7.56 (judge) and 41 vs 21 human pair wins; CBS 45% vs 29%; QDAIF human QD 0.772 vs 0.767.
limits: Cross-paper comparison; metrics and tasks differ, so it is a reading, not a measured effect.
agent_relevance: Rule for S3: use search hard where a check exists; elsewhere use few candidates plus a filter and keep cost low.

source: Cross-paper reading of c03, c04 and c19
finding: Reframing before searching: Nair et al. affordance text and MacGyver Div-Conv both change the representation of the problem (functions needed, uses listed) and both gave gains.
numbers: Nair: general gain, per-model values in a figure only. MacGyver: +6.5 points efficient solutions for GPT-4 with Div-Conv.
limits: Both are small. Different tasks and prompts.
agent_relevance: Add a short what-function-is-needed step at the start of open S3 search.

source: Cross-paper reading of c08, c11, c14, c15
finding: Failure modes when search uses a proxy score: ELM Radial seed exploited physics quirks; AI Scientist hallucinated experimental details; QDAIF gain over a fixed prompt faded in human evaluation.
numbers: ELM: Radial seed dropped from later stages. AI Scientist: failure list includes hallucinated hardware. QDAIF human quality 3.9 vs 4.133 for Fixed-Few-Shot.
limits: Collected from separate papers.
agent_relevance: Guardrail: any score the loop itself produces can be gamed; add an independent check before accepting a novel candidate.

source: Cross-paper reading of c04, c07, c17
finding: Cost side: tree search costs about as many tokens as 100 independent CoT trials but beat best-of-100 on Game of 24 (74% vs 49%). EoH needs thousands of queries where FunSearch reported about a million.
numbers: ToT 5.5k completion tokens vs 6.7k for 100 CoT; success 74% vs 49%. EoH vs FunSearch queries: thousands vs about 1 million.
limits: Costs from the ToT cost table and EoH text; prices change.
agent_relevance: Budget argument for S3: structured search beats the same tokens spent on blind resampling when the evaluator is good.

source: Search note: 2025-2026 coverage gap
finding: Search of arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs for 2025-2026 LLM studies of exploratory creativity as search returned nothing usable (empty or rate-limited). The WebSearch quota was used up.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: This is a gap in coverage, not proof that none exist. C04.01 already holds UoT, CreativeBench and Bhushan et al. for 2025-2026.
agent_relevance: Treat 2025-2026 coverage as incomplete. Re-run when the search quota refills.

source: Replication check of Nair et al. (2024)
finding: No independent replication or citing experiment of the founding position paper was located in this session. The code repo is listed in the paper and was not opened.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Citation search failed (rate limit).
agent_relevance: Do not count the Nair experiment as established.
